Working alongside the Data Protection Officer, you'll support Marley Risk Consultants in meeting its obligations under the UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018. You'll co-ordinate Data Subject Access Requests, maintain accurate data protection records and registers, support Data Protection Impact Assessments and monitor the Data Protection inbox.

You'll help ensure requests, enquiries and potential incidents are logged, progressed and retained correctly. Working across the business, you'll gather information securely, monitor statutory deadlines, identify gaps or risks and escalate urgent, sensitive or higher-risk matters promptly to the Data Protection Officer.

Key Responsibilities:
- Support the day-to-day administration of Data Subject Access Requests, ensuring requests are logged accurately, statutory deadlines are tracked, a clear audit trail is maintained and risks of delay are escalated.

- Review documents and identify information that may require redaction or exemption, referring final decisions and approval to the Data Protection Officer.
- Assist with reviewing DSAR material and preparing accurate, complete and timely responses for approval.
- Maintain accurate data protection logs and registers, including the personal data breach log, DPIA register and DSAR log, checking for missing, overdue or inconsistent entries.
- Monitor and manage the Data Protection inbox by triaging correspondence, recording actions, assigning or escalating matters and retaining completed items appropriately.
- Identify urgent, sensitive or higher-risk matters, including potential personal data breaches, complaints, regulatory correspondence and requests approaching statutory deadlines.
- Prepare complete case folders, check them against relevant records and promptly notify the Data Protection Officer of missing information, correspondence or actions.
- Support the initial recording and assessment of suspected personal data breaches, ensuring relevant information is captured and escalated in line with procedure.
- Support routine data protection queries, staff guidance, awareness activities and DPIAs, referring matters requiring formal advice or decision-making to the Data Protection Officer.

What We're Looking For:

We're looking for someone who can manage detailed administrative processes, protect confidential information and keep accurate records while working to statutory deadlines. You'll be methodical, proactive and comfortable working independently within agreed procedures, with the judgement to recognise when escalation is required.

Experience
- Practical knowledge of the UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and secure personal data handling principles.
- Experience supporting or managing DSARs, including logging, information gathering, review, redaction, deadline monitoring and preparation of responses.
- Experience handling sensitive and confidential information securely within organisational systems.
- Experience supporting the recording, initial assessment and escalation of suspected personal data breaches and contributing to DPIAs.
- Experience working across business areas to obtain, review and organise information within agreed timescales.
- Experience using Microsoft 365 or similar case and document-management systems to maintain accurate records, actions and audit trails.

Skills & Expertise

You'll bring:
- Strong organisational and administrative skills, excellent attention to detail and the ability to prioritise competing deadlines.
- Clear and professional written and verbal communication skills.
- Practical understanding of DSAR administration, secure information handling, redaction principles, statutory deadline monitoring and accurate record keeping.
- Confidence using Microsoft 365 and associated workflow tools.
- The ability to work independently within agreed procedures and recognise when formal advice or escalation is required.
- A discreet, dependable and collaborative approach to sensitive information and stakeholder relationships.
- Knowledge of DPIAs, records of processing activities, personal data breach management and ICO guidance is desirable.

Why Join Marley Risk Consultants?

At Marley, we're passionate about creating an environment where our people can make an impact, develop their expertise and help shape the way we work.

This is an opportunity to build practical experience across a broad range of data protection activity while supporting a function that protects individuals, strengthens governance and enables responsible business decisions. You'll be encouraged to contribute ideas, improve processes and help embed good data protection practice across the organisation.

You'll be joining a collaborative business where your voice matters, with opportunities to learn, develop and build your career alongside people committed to doing the right thing.

If you're looking for a role where you can make a difference, take ownership and support a strong culture of privacy and accountability, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Receptionist
description: The Reception Team is the first point of contact for patients and visitors attending our busy clinics and imaging services. Reporting to the Team Lead, you will be part of a supportive team working closely with healthcare professionals and administrative colleagues across the charity to ensure an exceptional patient experience. You will be responsible for managing the patient arrival process using our patient administration systems, providing clear information about appointments, taking payments, and directing patients to the appropriate departments. The role also involves supporting visiting consultants, booking appointments, preparing clinical documentation, processing correspondence, and responding to telephone and email enquiries. As the face of Cobalt, you will help create a welcoming and professional environment for patients and visitors. Confidence in using IT systems, excellent organisational skills, and a willingness to learn are essential. This is a 30-hour per week position worked on a rotational shift basis across the week, including regular Saturday working, with early, mid and late shifts. There is also the opportunity for a part-time Saturday position. You will have previous experience in a customer-facing or administrative role, ideally within a healthcare setting, and be confident working in a busy environment where attention to detail is essential. Strong IT skills and the ability to quickly learn new systems are important for success in this role. You will be an excellent communicator with a professional and friendly telephone manner, able to explain information clearly and sensitively to patients and visitors. You will enjoy working collaboratively as part of a team, building positive relationships with colleagues and providing outstanding customer service. A meticulous approach to accuracy, strong organisational skills, and the ability to maintain confidentiality at all times are essential. Your positive attitude and commitment to patient care will help contribute to a welcoming and supportive environment for all. Join our friendly Reception Team and play a key role in delivering an outstanding experience for patients attending our imaging and diagnostic services. As the first point of contact, you will welcome patients and visitors, manage appointments and enquiries, process payments, maintain accurate records, and provide administrative support to clinicians and colleagues across the charity. We're looking for someone with excellent communication and customer service skills, strong attention to detail, confidence using IT systems, and the ability to remain professional and organised in a busy environment. Previous experience in a customer-facing role is essential, with healthcare experience desirable. This is a 30-hour per week position worked on a rotational shift basis, including regular Saturday working. A part-time Saturday-only opportunity is also available.
